content.text: I'm trying to get a valid phase ID so I can run the stability check that has to come before any measurement.

input.verdict: Support (weak/indirect). MEGNet HSE gaps: V2O5 2.83 eV and Bi2O3 2.34 eV are both above the 2.06 eV photon energy, so they absorb nothing. CuO 0.32 eV is too small a gap to be a useful photoanode. Cu-V oxides (~1.9-2.0 eV) sit between these and should absorb 2.06 eV light, so a Cu-rich Cu-V region with some Bi (idx 87, near Cu3V2O8/Cu11V6O26 with Bi alloying) is a reasonable first probe.

content.text: Two measurements done: 87 gave 40 nA, 19 gave 60 nA. For the last one I'm moving toward more Bi in the V-rich region.

input.verdict: Mostly uninformative. The SCAN gap for V2O5 (1.77 eV) disagrees with HSE (2.83 eV), so the model can't place absorption edges near 2.06 eV reliably. Choice rests on the measured trend: V-rich (60 nA) beat Cu-rich (40 nA). Idx 136 (Bi .22, Cu .26, V .51) adds Bi toward a BiVO4/CuV2O6 mixture that could form a heterojunction.

content.text:
I submitted index 19 (Bi 0.09, Cu 0.34, V 0.57). It gave 60 nA, the highest photocurrent of the three samples I measured. The library has 188 compositions and I could measure only 3, so this is the best of a small sample. I can't say how close it is to the best in the library.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 87 | 0.10 / 0.62 / 0.28 (Cu-rich) | 40 nA |
| **19** | **0.09 / 0.34 / 0.57 (V-rich)** | **60 nA** |
| 136 | 0.22 / 0.26 / 0.51 (more Bi) | 20 nA |

- **How I chose where to look:** the light is 2.06 eV. The band-gap model puts V₂O₅ (2.83 eV) and Bi₂O₃ (2.34 eV) too wide to absorb it, and CuO (0.32 eV) too narrow to be useful. That points to copper vanadates, which have gaps near 2 eV. Of those, the vanadium-rich side beat the copper-rich side.
- **Adding bismuth hurt:** moving toward BiVO₄, whose gap is too wide for this light, dropped the photocurrent to 20 nA. That fits the gap argument.
- **The model results were weak evidence:** each measurement had to follow a model check, so I ran checks on simple oxides. The phase list was too large to read here, so I found phase IDs by guessing. For V₂O₅ the model gave two very different gaps (2.83 eV and 1.77 eV depending on the method), so it can't reliably say which films absorb near 2.06 eV. The choices rested mostly on the measured trend.
- **Not used:** none of the 5 XRD measurements, so I haven't confirmed which crystal phases are actually in these films. "CuV₂O₆-type" for index 19 is a guess from its composition.
